query: Why do some travel expenses get declined, and which factors contribute the most?

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: Flags travel-related expenses, which the query already scopes to ('travel expenses'). It functions as a scoping/filter indicator rather than a treatment or confounder cause of declines.

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: The type/category of expense item is a candidate cause whose effect on decline could be attributed (some categories may be more likely declined).

per_column.name: expense_entry_origin
per_column.rationale: How the expense entered the system (automated vs manual/explicit) could plausibly influence both the category/handling of the expense and its likelihood of being declined.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Presence of a source reference could affect both entry origin/completeness and the decline decision, potentially a common cause; but it is closer to a data-completeness proxy and its role is weakly justified.

per_column.name: processing_lag_category
per_column.rationale: Processing delay likely lies on the path between how/when an expense is handled and the final decline decision (or is itself downstream of processing), so it is a mediator/outcome-adjacent variable, not a clean common cause.

per_column.name: department_group
per_column.rationale: Department plausibly causes both the type/pattern of expenses submitted and the decline rate (different policies/scrutiny), a genuine common cause surfaced from data.

per_column.name: asset_action_type
per_column.rationale: The kind of action (new acquisition, procurement, etc.) is another candidate cause whose effect on declines could be attributed.

judge.rationale: The added columns do supply candidate treatments (asset_category, asset_action_type) and several confounders surfaced from the data rather than the query (department_group is the strongest genuine common cause; expense_entry_origin and has_source_id are plausible but weaker). However, the set is muddied: is_travel_related merely restates the query scope, processing_lag_category is a mediator/outcome-adjacent variable that would bias attribution if adjusted for, and much of the schema appears oriented to asset/procurement rather than a clean treatment-vs-confounder separation around declines. The causal-estimation structure is partially realised but confounder quality is moderate at best.
